question: Why is time unnecessary for explaining action and its limiting conditions?
premises: If one thing has one limiting condition, unity alone does not require time.
If difference arises within action or its condition, that difference is explained internally.
Time adds no explanatory function in either case.
inference: Time is explanatorily redundant with respect to action and its conditions.
uncertainties: The token '(?)' marks a textual uncertainty in the transmitted reading.
plain_english: If a single thing has a single limiting condition, its unity does not require time; and if difference belongs to action or to the condition itself, that is explained internally, so time serves no purpose.
